content: A daily dose of 1 mg of folic acid may mask the symptoms of pernicious anemia. While hematological remission can be achieved, irreversible nerve damage may continue to progress. This product should only be used under the supervision of a qualified healthcare provider. Folic acid is classified as Pregnancy Category A, indicating that controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. During lactation, folic acid is distributed into breast milk in amounts sufficient to meet the daily requirements of an infant. Folate is naturally present in various foods, particularly in leafy green vegetables. L-methylfolate is a medical nutritional supplement used to address conditions associated with folate deficiency. It is specifically utilized for the dietary management of low plasma or low red blood cell folate levels. Deplin is a medical nutritional supplement that provides the body with folate. Patients who become pregnant while using this supplement should inform their healthcare provider immediately. Prolonged folic acid therapy may lead to a reduction in serum vitamin B12 levels. The peak plasma concentration of L-methylfolate is reached approximately one hour after administration. It is metabolized in the liver and primarily excreted through urine (90%), with trace amounts eliminated in feces. L-methylfolate is the primary biologically active isomer of folic acid and represents the main circulating form of folate in the body. Folic acid serves as a precursor to tetrahydrofolic acid, which functions as a cofactor in transformylation reactions. These reactions are essential for the biosynthesis of thymidylates and purines, which are critical components of nucleic acids. The exact mechanism by which L-methylfolate acts as an adjunct therapy in depression remains unknown.
